stage_b_review_note: Pinned 2543–2553: for Noetherian R, ideal I having FINITE projective dimension and conormal I/I² finite LOCALLY FREE over R/I, I is a regular ideal, i.e. Zariski locally at primes over I generated by a regular sequence. Stage A expands the standard local definition and retains all prerequisites.
statement:
A regular ideal $I$ of a commutative ring $R$ means that for every prime $\mathfrak p\supset I$ there is a localization $R_g$, $g\notin\mathfrak p$, such that $I_g$ is generated by a regular sequence (More on Algebra, definition at L8101–8114).
Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring. Let $I \subset R$ be an ideal
which has finite projective dimension and such that $I/I^2$ is
finite locally free over $R/I$. Then $I$ is a regular ideal
(the local regular-sequence definition provided in the context note).
